evidence.text: Initially, we start by acquiring all the materials from the MP database based on its API, resulting in a total of 1,54,718 entries saved in a JSON file as the Python dictionary object.
The dataset used in this study is publicly available from the MaterialsProject database: https://next-gen.materialsproject.org/.

Ultimately, through excluding the materials containing hydrogen, lanthanides, and actinides, and conducting structural analysis, we further obtain 2675 three-dimensional (3D) crystal structures without calculation errors. These materials constitute the first-level dataset for our in-depth investigations.

Since the materials with a high likelihood of possessing relatively low κL tend to group into the two clusters of C1 and C2, the exploration scope for finding materials with low κL is reduced from 2675 materials to 704 materials, narrowing by approximately three-quarters. As a result, these two problem-speciﬁc clusters (C1 and C2) further constitute our second-level dataset.

The basic information and corresponding κPET values of the resulting 661 materials are then stored in a local database using MongoDB64, serving as a valuable repository to retrieve data and prioritize detailed theoretical and experimental investigations.

Given the success of unsupervised learning in signiﬁcantly reducing the broad material search space, it has become feasible to further extend the second-level dataset into a labeled repository of thermal conductivity through HTC at affordable computational costs.
